document_kind: Hand-written summary of the cited LANUK pages (not a copy). Wording is ours; check the originals before relying on it.

status_nrw.text: Fully naturalised in NRW ('als Agriophyt ... überall eingebürgert'); strong spread since the 1970s.
Classified by LANUK as invasive: high reproductive potential (early seed production, stump sprouting, root suckers) and high dispersal potential.
NRW biodiversity monitoring reports a rising trend since 2006.
Not on the EU list of invasive alien species of Union concern (LANUK find points carry 'nicht Unionsliste'). There is therefore no EU-regulation reporting duty; reporting to LANUK is voluntary.

identification.text: Leaves 5–12 cm, pointed, finely serrated, leathery and conspicuously glossy — the shine separates it from other Prunus species.
Leaf underside with a dense hair felt (LANUK wording 'dichter Haarfilz'); check the exact position of the hairs in the original.
White, fragrant flowers, about 30 per cylindrical raceme (6–15 cm), upright then drooping; opens after leaf emergence.
Cherries 8–10 mm, green → black-red → black, with a persistent calyx at the base.

lookalikes.hint: Flowers noticeably earlier; LANUK names it as the main confusion species.

impacts.text: Forms a dense, closed shrub layer that strongly restricts tree regeneration in forests.
As a semi-shade species it regenerates ahead of light-demanding oak, rowan and pine and shades them out.
Allelopathic substances additionally inhibit root growth of other seedlings.
Most problematic for nature conservation in open pine and oak woodland on sandy soils.

lanuk_prioritisation_context.note: LANUK describes where control measures should have priority. The prototype only shows which of these facts are known for an observation. It never turns them into a recommendation; decisions stay with the responsible experts.

criteria.text: In or directly next to areas with rare and endangered species or biotopes.

lanuk_prioritisation_context.follow_up: LANUK states that complete eradication is unrealistic and that treated areas need follow-up monitoring for several years (stump sprouting, root fragments).
